files.note: A Lanczos resample of the input to 8192x4096, JPEG quality 90. The input is kept in data/lookdev/sources, outside git, and pinned by its SHA-256 in the source. Rebaked byte for byte on 2026-11-04 with this repository's locked dependencies.

A Lanczos resample of the input to 8192x4096, with the dim base layer NASA blended in removed by a luminance smoothstep from 0.10 to 0.55, JPEG quality 92. Relative brightness follows NASA's stretched visualization, not calibrated radiance. The input is kept in data/lookdev/sources, outside git, and pinned by its SHA-256 in the source. Rebaked byte for byte on 2026-11-04 with this repository's locked dependencies.

Byte-identical to https://cdn.eso.org/images/large/eso0932a.jpg as downloaded on 2026-11-04; ESO does not distribute the 800-megapixel original. A mosaic of almost 300 fields, each shot four times over 2008 and 2009, stitched by Frederic Tapissier. Plate carree, 360 by 180 degrees, with the galactic plane horizontal; its axes sit 3.78 degrees from galactic, so the renderers sample it through eso0932a_registration.json. The pixels are unchanged; the shader grades the image for display (black level 0.042, power 1.52 and a warm tint). It shows Venus at RA 23h19m, Dec -3.9 and Jupiter at RA 19h30m, Dec -21.9, where they stood when their fields were shot; the repository's ephemeris puts Venus within 0.06 degrees of that point on 2009-01-22 and Jupiter within 0.04 degrees on 2008-06-09 (tests/integration/test_sky_registration.py), dates of agreement rather than capture dates from ESO. Both planets stay in the image, unretouched, and the sky layer's disclosure names them.

The panorama's registration to the catalog stars (docs/science/SKY_PANORAMA_REGISTRATION.md): a rotation from galactic plus a vertical offset, then a smoothed table of the remaining offsets, fitted to 5,021 isolated stars to magnitude 6 from the core tiles of layers 0 and 1, which it pins by one SHA-256, and checked on held-out stars. The panorama's pixels are not changed. `--verify` refits and compares byte for byte on the machine that made the file; tests/integration/test_sky_registration.py allows for platform rounding.
